'''Michael John Dorff''' (often referred to as Coach Dorff<ref>{{Cite web |last=Christensen |first=Media Contact: Andrea |date=2018-02-02 |title=Meet the new president of math |url=https://news.byu.edu/news/meet-new-president-math |access-date=2025-01-17 |website=News |language=en}}</ref>) is a mathematician at [[Brigham Young University]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Home - BYU |url=https://www.byu.edu/ |access-date=2025-04-29 |website=BYU Home Site |language=en}}</ref> known for his work in [[undergraduate research]], promoting careers in math, popularizing mathematics, and [[harmonic mapping]]s.

==Life and career==

Michael Dorff received his BA in Mathematics Education from [[Brigham Young University]]<ref name=":0" /> in 1986. He received his MS from [[University of New Hampshire]] in 1992 followed by a Ph.D. in Mathematics from [[University of Kentucky]] in 1997.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Michael Dorff - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=14757 |access-date=2025-04-29 |website=mathgenealogy.org}}</ref> He taught at [[University of Missouri-Rolla]] as an assistant professor in the Department of Math and Statistics from 1997-2000 when he was hired by [[Brigham Young University]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Home - BYU |url=https://www.byu.edu/ |access-date=2025-04-29 |website=BYU Home Site |language=en}}</ref> as an assistant professor in the Department of Mathematics. Dorff became a full professor at [[BYU]]<ref name=":0" /> in 2011. He was the Chair of the Department of Mathematics at [[BYU]]<ref name=":0" /> from 2015–2019 and 2025-2028.

He is a Fellow of the American Mathematical Society (AMS), a CUR Fellow ([[Council on Undergraduate Research]]), and a Fulbright Scholar. He was awarded with the MAA Gung and Hu Award for Distinguished Service to Mathematics (2024), BYU University Professor (2023), BYU Lawrence K. Egbert Teaching and Learning Faculty Fellowship (2015), MAA Deborah and Franklin Tepper Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics (2010), and BYU Karl G. Maeser Excellence in Teaching Award (2010).

His mathematics research area is geometric function theory, and he has expertise in preparing students for careers in BIG (business, industry, and government) and in undergraduate research.<ref name="math.byu.edu">{{Cite web |last=Dorff |first=Michael |date=1 January 2015 |title=Michael Dorff - Professor, Mathematics |url=https://mathdept.byu.edu/~mdorff/ |access-date=}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
* 2025–2027, Member of the Mathematical Sciences Education Board for the National Academies of Science
* 2021–2024, Executive Director of Transforming Post-Secondary Education in Mathematics (TPSE Math)
* 2020, Council on Undergraduate Research (CUR) Fellows Award.<ref name="math.byu.edu" />
* 2019–2020, President of the [[Mathematical Association of America]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Election {{!}} Mathematical Association of America |url=https://www.maa.org/election |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240405215533/https://maa.org/election |archive-date=2024-04-05 |access-date=2025-04-29 |website=www.maa.org |language=en}}</ref>
* 2015, The "Mathematics Programs that Make a Difference" from the AMS for CURM.<ref name="math.byu.edu"/>
* 2013–2024 Co-founder and co-director of PIC Math (Preparation for Industrial Careers in the Mathematical Sciences)
* 2012–2015, The Lawrence K. Egbert Teaching and Learning Faculty Fellowship at [[Brigham Young University]].<ref name="math.byu.edu"/>
* 2012, Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS :: Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |url=http://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows.cgi |access-date=2025-04-29 |website=www.ams.org}}</ref>
* 2010, The Karl G. Maeser Excellence in Teaching Award at [[Brigham Young University]].<ref name="math.byu.edu"/>
* 2010, The [[Haimo Award|Deborah and Franklin Tepper Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics]].<ref name="newsnet">{{Cite web |date=2009-01-07 |title=BYU's Michael Dorff wins top mathematics teaching award |url=https://news.byu.edu/news/byus-michael-dorff-wins-top-mathematics-teaching-award |access-date=2025-04-29 |website=News |language=en}}</ref>
* 2007–2017, Founder and director of the Center for Undergraduate Research in Mathematics (CURM)

==Selected publications==
'''Books:'''
* M. Dorff, A. Henrich, and L. Pudwell. A Mathematician's Practical Guide to Mentoring Undergraduate Research. MAA Press: An Imprint of the American Mathematical Society, 2019.
* M. Brilleslyper, M. Dorff, J. McDougall, J. Rolf, L. Schaubroeck, R. Stankewitz, and K. Stephenson. Explorations in Complex Analysis. Math. Assoc. of America. Washington, DC, 2012.

'''Research Papers:'''
* M. Brilleslyper, J. Brooks, M. Dorff, R. Howell and L. Schaubroeck. “Zeros of a one-parameter family of harmonic trinomials,” accepted for publication in Proc. Amer. Math. Soc., 2020.
* Z. Boyd*, M. Dorff, M. Nowak, M. Romney, and M. Woloszkiewicz. “Univalency of convolutions of harmonic mappings,” Appl. Math. Comput. 234 (2014), 326–332.
* M. Dorff, M. Nowak, and M. Wołoszkiewicz. “Convolutions of harmonic convex mappings.” Complex Var. Elliptic Equ. 57 (2012), no. 5, 489–503.
* M. Dorff and M. Nowak. “Landau's Theorem for planar harmonic mappings.” Comput. Methods Funct. Theory 4 (2004), no. 1, 151–158.
* M. Dorff. “Convolutions of planar harmonic convex mappings.” Complex Var. Theory Appl. 45 (2001), 263–271.
